cards.back: The probability that a genotype produces its associated phenotype under specified conditions.
The degree or form in which a genotype-associated phenotype appears among affected individuals.
A cross to a homozygous recessive tester used to reveal the gametes produced by an individual of unknown or heterozygous genotype.
A mapping unit corresponding approximately to a 1% recombination frequency for short intervals.
A DNA sequence that influences expression of a gene on the same DNA molecule.
Restoration of a phenotype by reintroducing the implicated function after a perturbation.
Nonrandom association of alleles at different loci in a population.
Statistical and functional methods used to narrow an associated region to likely causal variants.
p = (2 n(AA) + n(Aa)) / 2N; the denominator counts allele copies.
p², 2pq, q² under random union of gametes: random mating, no selection, migration or mutation, large population, one population sampled.
F = 1 − H_obs/H_exp; one marker suggests genotyping error, many markers suggest structure or inbreeding.
q = √incidence and carriers = 2pq under Hardy–Weinberg; consanguinity biases q upward.
h² = V_A / V_P for a population in an environment; not a per-person fraction and not a measure of changeability.
h² = 2(r_MZ − r_DZ), c² = 2r_DZ − r_MZ, e² = 1 − r_MZ, assuming equal environments and additivity.
PGS = Σ β_i g_i; accuracy is variance explained in an independent sample, and r = √R².
Scores trained in one ancestry usually predict less well in others because allele frequencies and linkage differ.
Crossing to a recessive tester makes each progeny phenotype reveal the gamete from the heterozygous parent.
The rarest classes are double crossovers; the locus that differs from parental in them is the middle one.
Expected DCO = r₁ × r₂ × N; coefficient of coincidence = observed/expected; I = 1 − CoC.
Observed r undercounts multiple exchanges and cannot exceed 0.5; Haldane d = −½ ln(1 − 2r) assumes no interference.
Knockout cuts DNA; CRISPRi blocks transcription without cutting; RNAi degrades transcripts; each can hit off-targets.
Non-targeting control, two independent reagents and rescue with a resistant construct.
ΔCt = target − reference; ΔΔCt = perturbed − control; relative expression = 2^(−ΔΔCt) if efficiency ≈ 100% and the reference is stable.
Independent biological replicates are the unit; n ≈ 2(z₁ + z₂)²σ²/δ² per group is a normal approximation that runs low at small n; wells from one transfection are technical replicates.
Relevance, independence from confounders, exclusion restriction (no horizontal pleiotropy).
β_XY = β_ZY/β_ZX; SE ≈ SE(β_ZY)/|β_ZX| for strong instruments.
F ≈ (β_ZX/SE)²; below about 10 is weak and biases estimates.
MR estimates a lifelong genetic shift; check heterogeneity and robust estimators.
9:7 complementary genes; 9:3:4 recessive epistasis; 12:3:1 dominant epistasis; 15:1 duplicate genes.
Cross two recessive mutants: wild-type F1 = different genes (complement); mutant F1 = same gene.
Use counts; df = classes − 1 − estimated parameters; 5% critical values 3.84 (1 df) and 5.99 (2 df).
A double mutant resembling one single mutant suggests that gene acts downstream; daf-16 is needed for daf-2 longevity in worms.
Affected males through carrier females; never father to son; each son of a carrier mother 1/2 affected.
Posterior = prior × likelihood / Σ(prior × likelihood); prior 1/2 with three unaffected sons gives 1/9.
Each unaffected son multiplies the carrier odds by 1/2 (with complete penetrance); it lowers but does not exclude risk.
Incomplete penetrance, new mutations and X-inactivation mosaicism all change pedigree-based estimates.
MI: no normal products (2 disomic, 2 nullisomic). MII in one cell: 2 normal, 1 disomic, 1 nullisomic.
At least 5% of clinically recognized pregnancies; the leading genetic cause of pregnancy loss.
RR = risk₁/risk₀ shows strength; RD = risk₁ − risk₀ shows how many extra cases per 1000.
Near the centromere: two different parental alleles = meiosis I error; two identical alleles = meiosis II error.
Rate = events per cell division; frequency = fraction of mutant cells, inflated by early jackpots.
m = −ln(fraction of cultures with no mutants); rate ≈ m / divisions per culture.
Excess variance across independent cultures (not aliquots) shows mutations arise before selection.
Adult stem cells of several tissues gain roughly 40 mutations per year; accumulation alone does not prove causation.
CPM = gene reads / total reads × 10⁶; compare normalized values, never raw counts.
log₂(treated/control): +1 doubles, −1 halves; noisy for low-count genes.
Sort p-values; largest k with p(k) ≤ (k/m)q; call the k smallest. Controls the false discovery rate.
If a group is processed entirely in its own batch, batch and group effects cannot be separated; balance and record batches.
Mean dosage (0 to 2 effect alleles per person) divided by 2 is the effect-allele frequency.
OR = (a/b)/(c/d) from effect and other allele counts in cases and controls; χ² = Σ(O − E)²/E with 1 df.
If cases and controls differ in ancestry and allele frequencies differ by ancestry, a pooled signal can be spurious; stratify or adjust.
A multiple-testing threshold controls chance findings, not confounded ones; a corrected hit is a candidate to replicate.
PIP(i) = BF(i) / Σ BF(j) under one causal variant and equal priors; a 95% credible set sums to at least 0.95.
In heterozygotes, unequal RNA reads show something on the haplotype acts in cis; check DNA ratios and mapping bias.
Association → region; fine-mapping → candidates; chromatin → cell type; ASE → haplotype; editing → variant; rescue → phenotype in the system.
Ancestry, cell-type composition, processing batch and linkage disequilibrium must be addressed before naming a causal variant.
